subject: physical-education
title: Concept model A: strength, mobility, and bodyweight practice
essentialQuestion: Which activities would I still be doing at thirty?
materials: whatever the trialed activities require; free and household options are always offered
privacySafeScenario: Trial three individual or dual activities, evaluate each against enjoyment, access, cost, and sustainability, and justify which one is worth continuing.
studentTask: Learner applies strength, mobility, and bodyweight practice in a new situation at a self-set intensity and records what they did, noticed, and would adjust.
knowledgeCheck: In one concise response, explain the key idea behind strength, mobility, and bodyweight practice and name one adjustment for the next session.
completionCriteria: The learner completes or fully describes the strength, mobility, and bodyweight practice task using a version their body and setting allow.
The learner gives a cue, principle, tactic, or documented process rather than an unexplained result.
The learner self-assesses against the stated criteria and identifies one next adjustment.
adaptationChoices: Every activity family includes a seated, low-impact, indoor, and zero-cost option, and a learner may design a substitute activity that meets the same description.
extensionChallenge: Apply strength, mobility, and bodyweight practice under a new constraint, in a different activity, or teach the cue to someone else — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
Every activity family includes a seated, low-impact, indoor, and zero-cost option, and a learner may design a substitute activity that meets the same description.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to notice or try one safe, optional example of strength, mobility, and bodyweight practice in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
